Design review — sprint `2026-09-20-evidence-pipeline-integrity`, review_run_id 09eec6bf-462c-416b-a202-e0b8d949f145, mode: design. Read-only; no files written. Input hashes re-verified on disk: review-packet.md = 15b67edd…ef12f, design.md = b205ee91…c481a4b (both match the dispatch).

Findings

- [P1] design.md:20 (HOW, `|` / `|&` "but not `||`") — The exclusion wording is ambiguous and, read literally ("command contains `||` ⇒ not a pipeline"), reopens the exact false-PASS the sprint targets. `npm test | tail -8 || echo done` contains a real pipe **and** `||`; under the literal reading it is classified as "unpiped", keeps existing status semantics, and still records `pass`. Evidence: the command is classified as test evidence by the live classifier (`vibeCoding/claude/9.9.9/.claude/hooks/_input-binding.cjs:16` + `:8-14`; verified by running `classifyValidation("npm test | tail -8 || echo done") -> "test"`), and `vibeCoding/claude/9.9.9/.claude/hooks/evidence-collector.cjs:52-53` returns `"pass"` for it. The rule must be stated token-wise ("a `|` that is not the second char of `||` and not `|&`"), not text-contains-wise.

- [P1] design.md:27-33 (Acceptance Criteria) vs roadmap row 4 — Roadmap `q12-batch2-production-gaps/roadmap.md` row 4 asks for "可证明的 pipefail/**首段退出状态**语义", but the design only covers the pipe operator. The identical last-command masking via sequence/background operators is left wide open and is not listed as a non-goal: `npm test || true`, `npm test; echo done`, and `npm test &` all classify as test evidence (verified against the live classifier) and all yield exit 0 → `evidence-collector.cjs:52-53` → `result: pass` with failing tests. `set -o pipefail` does not help any of these. AC2 is scoped to "the same pipelines", so the AC set is internally consistent but under-covers the roadmap row it claims to close. Decide before impl: extend the policy to "the classified validation token must be the last executed segment", or write an explicit non-goal + roadmap follow-up row (this changes AC2/AC3 wording and the test matrix, so it cannot be deferred to impl).

- [P1] design.md:35-43 (File Structure Plan) — Omits `vibeCoding/pi-agent/plugin/extensions/cc-core/_input-binding.cjs`, which is **byte-identical** to the CC file (both sha256 `30a88e4bf884800b4614be77d04d2530ed88f343797ed4416bec83e0c5705e4b`) and is live code: `vibeCoding/pi-agent/plugin/extensions/athena-gates.ts:19,63` runs `cc-core/pre-bash-guard.cjs` (also byte-identical, sha `3a9ee518…`), which `require`s `./_input-binding.cjs` at `pre-bash-guard.cjs:357`. `athena-gates.ts:4` states the invariant explicitly: "cc-core/*.cjs 复用 (与 claude/9.9.9 同源)". Touching only the CC copy silently breaks that invariant, and no sync script exists (nothing under `vibeCoding/scripts/` references `pi-agent`; the only test hit is `vibeCoding/scripts/tests/athena999/test_state_review.py:267`, a doc-content check). Note the asymmetry is real and should be stated in the plan: Pi has **no** `evidence-collector.cjs`, so only the binding-module half applies to Pi. Planning doc-only Pi work (AC5) while leaving Pi's shared *code* stale is the inverted priority.

- [P1] design.md:21 ("Lexical rule (no shell AST)") vs `vibeCoding/claude/9.9.9/.claude/hooks/pre-bash-guard.cjs:129-144` and `vibeCoding/codex/9.9.9/.codex/hooks/pre-bash-guard.py:94-190` — A quote-aware operator tokenizer already exists in the same package on both platforms: it tracks `'`/`"`/backslash state and emits `&&`/`||` as distinct ops from `|` and `;` (`pre-bash-guard.cjs:140-143`; `pre-bash-guard.py:182`). Introducing a second, strictly weaker lexer duplicates the same operator-splitting logic (coding-standards DRY is P0) and is what creates the quoted-pipe false negatives: `go test -run 'A|B' ./...` and `pytest -k "a|b"` both classify as test evidence (verified) and would be downgraded to `unknown` despite containing no pipeline at all. The design's non-goal at :47 covers a heredoc/AST parser (slice #14), not reuse of the existing tokenizer. Design must record the reuse-vs-duplicate decision with the #14 boundary, or extract the tokenizer.

- [P1] design.md:29-32 (AC1/AC2 verification) vs `vibeCoding/scripts/tests/athena999/test_state_review.py:589,605,618,690` — Every existing hook-chain test feeds `tool_response={'exit_code':0,...}` to **both** platforms, so the CC branch that actually causes the production symptom (`evidence-collector.cjs:52-53`, the no-`exit_code` heuristic documented at `:49-51`) is never exercised today. If impl copies the existing pattern, AC1/AC2 will go green without ever covering the reported CC failure mode. The ACs must mandate a CC-shaped payload (`{stdout, stderr, interrupted:false}`, no `exit_code`) for the CC leg, plus a `PostToolUseFailure` leg for the "real failure stays fail" half. The chain itself (pre-bash-guard → evidence-collector → `parse_evidence_records`) is otherwise a proven fixture (`test_state_review.py:580-596`), and AC5 has an established three-platform doc-assertion precedent at `test_state_review.py:263-273`; all five ACs are testable through the real chain.

- [P2] design.md:21 (`set` statement rule) — "the last statement whose first word is `set` decides" is wrong against bash semantics in the safe direction, and imprecise in the other. `set -o pipefail; set -e; npm test | tail -8` really does have pipefail enabled, but the rule picks `set -e` (mentions neither `-o pipefail` nor `+o pipefail`) → downgrade to `unknown` → ship blocked on a correct command. Conversely `set -o pipefail -o errexit` may miss a trailing-token match. Precise rule: scan all `set` statements before the first pipe token in order; any `-o pipefail` / `-<flags>o pipefail` enables, any `+o pipefail` / `+<flags>o pipefail` disables, `set` statements mentioning neither are ignored. Cite https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/html_node/The-Set-Builtin.html alongside the Pipelines page already in design.md:15.

- [P2] design.md:23 (`unverifiable_reason` key name) — Collides semantically with the existing `binding_status: 'unverifiable'` axis (`_input-binding.cjs:96,100`). One record can legitimately carry `binding_status: unverifiable` (input drift) **and** `unverifiable_reason: pipeline_without_pipefail` (status provenance), which reads as one cause and is two. Prefer `result_reason` / `unknown_reason`. Also, the reason string `pipeline_without_pipefail` is factually wrong for the quoted-pipe false negatives noted above.

- [P2] `vibeCoding/codex/9.9.9/.codex/hooks/evidence-collector.py:146` vs `vibeCoding/claude/9.9.9/.claude/hooks/evidence-collector.cjs:96` — CX persists `redact(command)[:120]`, CC persists `command.slice(0,500)`. A 120-char truncation can cut the pipe or the `set -o pipefail` prefix out of the recorded evidence, so an operator (or any future gate-side re-derivation) cannot audit the policy decision from `evidence.yaml` on CX. AC3 claims CC/CX symmetry; the design should either state that symmetry is about the policy verdict only, or raise the CX limit.

- [P2] design.md:23 ("no gate change is needed") — **Claim verified TRUE.** Both gates read evidence by named field only, so an extra key is ignored: `delivery-gate.cjs:952-975` / `delivery-gate.py:638-666`; no `exactKeys` strictness is applied to evidence records (the strict path at `delivery-gate.cjs:826` is spec-gate user authorization). And `unknown` correctly fails to satisfy ship: `delivery-gate.cjs:247,269` ("unknown-only is insufficient") / `delivery-gate.py:863,899`, plus per-AC admissibility requires `result === "pass"` at `delivery-gate.cjs:996` / `delivery-gate.py:700`. Downgrade-to-unknown therefore blocks ship without a gate edit, and avoids contending with the serialized delivery-gate slices.

- [P2] design.md:23 (evidence YAML injection) — **Closed by existing serializers, with one constraint to state in the design.** Values are JSON-escaped on both sides (`evidence-collector.cjs:57-58,71`; `evidence-collector.py:151`), so newlines/quotes in a reason cannot forge a `result:` line; CX's global one-result-per-record check (`delivery-gate.py:873-875`) would also catch it. But CC emits the *key* unescaped (`evidence-collector.cjs:71`: `'    '+key+': '+yamlString(value)`), so the new field name must remain a hardcoded literal — worth one line in the design. Redaction is genuinely untouched by this change.

- [P2] design.md:30 (AC2 "can never produce `result: pass`") — Scope overclaim. The policy binds only collector-written records; `source_sha256`/`design_sha256`/`environment_sha256`/`artifact_sha256` are all agent-computable, so a hand-written `result: pass` record still survives `currentRecord` (`_input-binding.cjs:102-108`). That hole is roadmap #1's slice (外部写者 provenance). Reword AC2 to "no collector-written record can…" so the AC stays provable.

- [P2] design.md:25 + packet "Challenge points" #5 ("#13 regression-only") — **Claim verified TRUE.** Both collectors already implement the 1500-char threshold with 300-head / 1200-tail: `evidence-collector.cjs:39-41` (code-point aware via `[...redacted]`) and `evidence-collector.py:43-45`, and the behavior is already asserted end-to-end at `test_state_review.py:598-623` including the unicode non-truncation case. No second summary mechanism is being introduced; AC4 is correctly scoped to regression coverage. AC5's three target files all exist (`claude/9.9.9/.claude/skills/pace/references/gate-contracts.md`, `codex/9.9.9/.codex/skills/pace/references/gate-contracts.md`, `pi-agent/plugin/skills/pace/references/gate-contracts.md`); none currently mentions `pipefail`/`tail`/`tee`, so AC5 is real work and not fabricated platform symmetry. No over-engineering found: no new config/flag/extension point, no gate edit, and co-locating the policy beside `classifyValidation` in the input-binding module is the minimal placement given `evidence-collector` already imports it.

AC bijection: OK — empirically re-derived with the live gate: `acceptanceCriteria(design.md)` yields 5 criteria → `{AC1..AC5}`; `extractAcIds(review-packet.md)` yields `{AC1..AC5}`; missing=∅, extra=∅ (`delivery-gate.cjs:344-353`). Packet is 33 lines (limit 80, `delivery-gate.cjs:333`) and `source_design_sha256` matches design.md on disk. Caveat, not a bijection break: packet AC4's "Mechanism" cell ("existing redaction head/tail") drops design AC4's second clause ("no second summary option or duplicate collector path"); that clause only survives in Challenge point #5. Add it to the AC4 row so the reviewer-facing mapping is complete.

VERDICT: CONCERNS
